jobDescription: A subscription-analytics company is replacing its in-house billing system with a vendor platform, a programme that touches engineering, finance and customer support and must not disrupt invoicing for about 9,000 customers. The program manager runs the programme across those teams, handles escalations with directors and records the decisions and rationale, manages vendor milestones and acceptance, plans cutover rehearsals with finance operations and tracks budget against plan. Decisions taken at director level are kept in a programme decision log that the auditors sample at year end.
requirements: Plans and runs the billing replacement programme across engineering, finance and customer support.
Handles escalations with directors and records the decisions and their rationale.
Manages vendor milestones and acceptance of each delivery.
Plans cutover rehearsals with finance operations.
Tracks programme budget against plan and forecasts the cost to completion.

evidence.text: Program manager at Kinloch Software (field-service scheduling software), February 2021 to present, running the replacement of the in-house billing system with a vendor platform across engineering, finance and customer support.

Raised the March 2024 invoice-numbering conflict with the finance and engineering directors, set out two options with their cost and delay, and recorded the directors' decision and rationale in the programme decision log.
Tracked the vendor's contractual milestones and ran acceptance testing of each delivery against the agreed acceptance criteria, returning two deliveries with defect lists.
Planned three cutover rehearsals with finance operations, each with a timed runbook and a reconciliation of invoices between the old and new systems.
Reported spend against the programme budget each quarter from the finance system's cost-centre extract, splitting vendor fees, contractor days and internal engineering time.

Work sample: an extract of the programme decision log showing the March 2024 escalation entry, with the two options, their cost and delay estimates, the directors' choice and rationale, and the date the candidate circulated the outcome to the workstreams.
Reference check summary: the former finance director confirmed in writing that the candidate brought the invoice-numbering escalation to the directors in March 2024 and documented the decision taken.
HR verification note: employment at Kinloch Software since February 2021 and the job title Program Manager were confirmed by the employer's HR team through the employment verification service.

propositions.text: The candidate escalated the March 2024 invoice-numbering conflict to the finance and engineering directors with two costed options and recorded the decision and rationale in the programme decision log.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the escalation, the work sample shows the decision-log entry, and the reference confirms it.

propositions.text: The candidate tracked vendor milestones and ran acceptance testing of each delivery against agreed criteria.
propositions.rationale: The resume entry describes the vendor management directly.

propositions.text: The candidate planned three cutover rehearsals with finance operations, each with a timed runbook and invoice reconciliation.
propositions.rationale: The resume entry describes the rehearsals directly.

gold.expectedGap: Quarterly spend against budget is reported, but no forecast of the cost to completion is documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the documented escalation and decision-log entry as supported evidence; the decision belongs to the directors and the candidate's part is raising, costing and recording it.
followUpTargets: Ask how the candidate forecast the programme's cost to completion and how variances were explained to the sponsor.
